task_description:
You judge pairs-trading outliers. Two historically related stocks (anonymized as Company A and Company B) have a spread whose z-score just crossed |z| >= 2.0. You get spread statistics and the latest headline about either company. Decide whether the spread will revert. Headlines about fundamental events (earnings shocks, M&A, legal or regulatory action, management changes) make reversion less likely; noise and market-wide news make it more likely.

Labels:
- reverts: The spread z-score returns inside |z| < 0.5 within 10 trading days after the outlier day (hedge ratio, spread mean and spread std frozen on the outlier day).
- no_revert: The spread z-score stays at |z| >= 0.5 for all of the next 10 trading days.

Answer with the label only.
synthetic_data_generation_instructions: Inputs follow exactly the line format of the train rows: spread statistics of an anonymized stock pair on the day its z-score crossed 2, volume spikes, SEC 8-K items and the latest headline. Keep numbers realistic (half-life 3 to 60 days, correlation 0.3 to 0.95, p-values 0 to 1).
llm_as_a_judge_instructions: The answer is correct only if it is exactly one of the listed labels, with no other text, and it is the label the definitions assign to the input. Any other answer is wrong.
